{{Quote|And this is Vulpter, for goodness' sake&mdash;their security isn't exactly a ring of durasteel.|[[Lon Shevu]]|<ref name="Sacrificec" />}}
'''Vulpter''' was the third [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of the [[Vulpter system/Legends|Vulpter system]] in the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]], and the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Vulptereen/Legends|Vulptereen]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. Originally an unspoiled world with a wide array of [[Plant/Legends|flora]] and fauna, Vulpter was transformed over the [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]] into a massively polluted globe covered in waste and [[Factory/Legends|factories]]. This meant that the planet was unable to sustain itself in terms of agriculture, and was thus entirely reliant on importing [[Foodstuff/Legends|foodstuffs]] from other worlds. Vulpter was a noted producer of [[Starship/Legends|starships]], and was home to one of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] largest [[Podracer/Legends|podracer]] factories. Several corporations, such as [[Viper Sensor Intelligence Systems]] and [[Arakyd Industries/Legends|Arakyd Industries]], operated facilities on the planet.

Vulpter became part of the [[galactic community]] at large between [[20,000 BBY/Legends|20,000]] and [[15,000 BBY/Legends|15,000 BBY]]. The Vulptereens were among the founding members of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]], an allegiance that proved catastrophic for Vulpter's ecosystem. When the Federation seized control of the planet, the organization essentially turned the already-polluted world into an enormous junkyard. Following the establishment of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], Vulpter was [[Blockade/Legends|blockaded]] and cut off from all interplanetary trade, leading to widespread famine on the planet. It was not until the establishment of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] that Vulpter rejoined the galaxy. During the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], Vulpter was the site of a meeting between the heads of the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]] and the [[Confederation]], where [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Ben Skywalker]] [[Assassin/Legends|assassinated]] the Confederate [[Dur Gejjen|leader]].

==Description==
Vulpter was the only habitable [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Vulpter system/Legends|Vulpter system]] of the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]]. Despite being located near the center of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], it was historically considered insignificant by organizations such as the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] and the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], to the point where it was often omitted from maps. A local year on Vulpter lasted 391 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|standard days]], while each day consisted of 22.5 [[Standard hour/Legends|standard hours]]. The [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]], although heavily polluted, was breathable by most [[Species/Legends|species]], and the planet's temperature ranged from very cold to temperate.<ref name="wizards" /> Vulpter was situated on one end of the [[Carbonite Run/Legends|Carbonite Run]], a popular route used by [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] wishing to evade authorities on their way from the nearby planet [[Empress Teta/Legends|Empress Teta]].<ref name="wizards2" />

===Topography===
The planet was originally covered with grassy plains, forests, and a wide assortment of other types of terrain. Over the millennia the native [[Vulptereen/Legends|Vulptereen's]] intense focus on industrialization slowly turned Vulpter into a wasteland; polluted urban [[City/Legends|cities]], massive factories and waste pits became the dominant topographical features, and a thick smog enveloped the entire world. This caused agriculture to be unsustainable, with the inhabitants forced to import foodstuffs from other worlds. The situation was worsened when the Trade Federation seized control of the planet&mdash;the megacorporation turned the planet into a dumping ground for low quality goods and impoverished the natives. Immense underground caverns were dug by the Federation's [[driller machine]]s, and much of the planet's air and [[Water/Legends|water]] supply came to be considered toxic.<ref name="wizards" />

Trash was shot into [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] around Vulpter,<ref name="wizards" /> eventually forming massive, black belts around the world.<ref name="FFdeepcore">{{FactFile|7|PLA 1-6|Planets of the Core Worlds}}</ref> Of particular note was the [[Orbital Advertisement Ring]], an enormous advertisement billboard that surrounded the entire planet. The structure&mdash;consisting of [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometer]]-wide neon advertisements and assorted space debris&mdash;dominated Vulpter's skyline, and its shadow was large enough to ruin entire crop plantings&mdash;further damning agricultural efforts.<ref name="wizards" /> One of the largest [[Podracer/Legends|podracer]] factories in the galaxy was located on Vulpter,<ref name="NEGASp">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> making the sport popular enough for the Vulptereens to host an [[Vulpter Orbital|annual race]] in the Advertisement Field surrounding the planet. The major exports of Vulpter were vehicles and [[Starship/Legends|starships]], produced in the planet's many factories. In addition to food, the population relied on importing high technology and assorted consumer goods.<ref name="wizards" />

The acquired harsh climate of the planet ensured that five out of every six settlements were either abandoned or in gross disrepair&mdash;an example was [[Benoga]], a town that was both devoid of inhabitants and slowly falling apart. These empty cities often served as hiding places for criminals who wished to evade legal authorities, such as the [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] associate [[Harper Krass]]. Local rumor was that some of the abandoned settlements were haunted by [[Force ghost/Legends|ghosts]].<ref name="wizards" /> Inhabited cities included [[Charbi]]<ref name="Sacrificec" /> and [[Hpaq]].<ref name="HNN" />

===Government===
Vulpter fell, at various times, under the [[Politics/Legends|political]] hegemony of galaxy-spanning powers such as the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]],<ref name="TEAp" /> the Galactic Empire,<ref name="wizards" /> and [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire]].<ref name="TEAp" /> However, the only major organization to actively rule the planet was the Trade Federation.<ref name="wizards" /> Following the dissolution of the Federation in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]],<ref name="RHNSIE">{{InsiderCite|84|Republic HoloNet News Special Inaugural Edition 16:5:241}}</ref> Vulpter still retained some form of local government, which operated a police force and a navy. Organizations such as [[Charbi Port Authority]] somewhat unsuccessfully monitored customs and immigration to the planet.<ref name="Sacrificec" />

==History==
===Industrialization===
[[File:AAD-4.jpg|thumb|left|170px|A Viper employee adapting to Arakyd ownership.]]
As the native Vulptereen species made advances in technology, they took the first steps to industrialize their planet. Once a verdant world, the natives soon turned Vulpter into a polluted wasteland.<ref name="wizards" /> The world was discovered by the Galactic Republic somewhere between [[20,000 BBY/Legends|20,000]] and [[15,000 BBY/Legends|15,000 BBY]];<ref name="TEAp" /> subsequently, it joined the [[galactic community]].<ref name="wizards" /> Around [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]],<ref name="CSWEp314">{{CSWECite|III|314}}</ref> however, Vulpter was completely seized by the Federation through an internal power grab by [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidians]],<ref name="wizards" /> who viewed the planet purely as a factory<ref name="NEGASp" /> and its inhabitants as inferior. The Federation established its headquarters in the city of Benoga and set about impoverishing the Vulptereens and further industrializing the world.<ref name="wizards" />

In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the corporations [[Viper Sensor Intelligence Systems]] and [[Arakyd Industries/Legends|Arakyd Industries]], both based on Vulpter, were involved in a conflict. Arakyd asserted that Viper's [[XPLR-R]] prototype borrowed heavily from their [[Probe droid/Legends|probe droid]] designs. The situation was resolved when Arakyd&mdash;using sixty [[AAD-4 assault droid]]s and three [[XR-37]] [[Droid tank/Legends|tank units]]&mdash;raided and seized Viper's [[Viper Tower|Hpaq headquarters]]. Following the takeover, Viper Sensor Intelligence Systems was absorbed into Arakyd as a research and development division.<ref name="HNN" />

===Imperial Period===
Following the establishment of the Galactic Empire, [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] travel into the Deep Core was heavily restricted by the [[Imperial Hyperspace Security Net]], a complex and heavily monitored system ensuring that only authorized ships were allowed access to the region.<ref name="wizardsI">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20050414planetintro|text=Byss and the Deep Core|int=Byss and the Deep Core}} {{C|Introduction}}</ref> Perceived by the Empire as a world with no useful resources or strategic value, Vulpter was almost entirely cut off from the rest of the galaxy. Trade was actively prohibited, including the import of foodstuffs, upon which the population was entirely reliant. The ensuing famines and riots claimed millions of Vulptereen lives.<ref name="wizards" /> The population was also [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] in forced labor.<ref name="TEAp" /> The lack of Imperial attention led to Vulpter being used as a safe haven for operatives of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. When the Alliance managed to penetrate the Hyperspace Security Net, the planet became a major staging point for the organization's attacks on Imperial holdings in the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]]. In exchange for using the planet for military purposes, the Alliance supplied the inhabitants of Vulpter with much-needed foodstuffs and other resources.<ref name="wizards" />

===Rejoining the galaxy===
After the defeat of the Empire and the establishment of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], Vulpter rejoined the galactic community. The Vulptereens, back in control of their own world, set about transforming Vulpter into a viable manufacturing planet. The same ecosystem purification team responsible for cleaning up the ruined atmosphere of [[Duro/Legends|Duro]] was hired to mend Vulpter's broken ecology. Under their supervision, the planet slowly recovered from the centuries of reckless pollution.<ref name="wizards" />

During the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], the Vulpter city of Charbi served as the location for a secret meeting between [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] [[Chief of State (Galactic Alliance)|Chief of State]] [[Cal Omas]] and [[Confederation]] leader [[Dur Gejjen]] to bring an end to the conflict. The [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Ben Skywalker]], under orders from fellow Jedi [[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]], [[Assassin/Legends|assassinated]] Gejjen during the meeting, further souring the relationship between the two factions.<ref name="Sacrificec" />

==Inhabitants==
[[File:Bolt.jpg|thumb|Dud Bolt, a Vulptereen podracer]]
At one point, Vulpter had a total population of 421 million, 88 percent of which was Vulptereen.<ref name="wizards" /> The planet still had a population of between 100 and 500 million around [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]].<ref name="TEAp" />

===Vulptereen===
{{Main|Vulptereen/Legends}}
The dominant native species of Vulpter were the [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] Vulptereens&mdash;short, carnivorous [[Reptile/Legends|reptilians]] with long snouts<ref name="NEGASp" /> and a knack for manufacturing.<ref name="wizards" /> Uniquely, Vulptereens did not possess a centrally located [[Brain/Legends|brain]], putting them at risk of aphasia should they lose a [[Limb/Legends|limb]]. Vulptereen [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] had sub-standard depth perception, making the species reliant on echolocation to identify their surroundings.<ref name="NEGASp" /> The polluted environment of Vulpter meant that the Vulptereens were constantly plagued by [[Poison/Legends|toxin]]-based ailments. This also meant that, over time, the species developed a resistance to many of these toxins. Although completely impoverished and powerless under the Trade Federation, the Vulptereens were a hardy people that clung fast to their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]. The native tongue of the species was [[Vulpterish]].<ref name="wizards" />

===Immigrated species===
Also present on Vulpter were the [[Amaran/Legends|Amarans]], making up six percent of the planet's population. The Amarans were mainly under the employ of the Trade Federation as managers for the underground storage caverns. Most members of the species did not get along well with the Vulptereens. Additionally, small minorities of Neimoidians and [[Human/Legends|Humans]] called the planet home.<ref name="wizards" />

===Fauna===
The pollution-fueled destruction of Vulpter's ecosystem eradicated Vulpter's native wildlife. One of the few survivors was the non-sentient [[garbage hunter]] species; two meter long rodents with substantial spine ridges that quickly adapted to living in the planet's many junkyards. When sneaking up on potential prey, garbage hunters would submerge themselves in garbage, revealed only by their spine ridges sticking out above the surface.<ref name="wizards" />

==Locations==
===Benoga===
{{Main|Benoga}}
Benoga was once a large and heavily populated city, home to the Trade Federation's corporate headquarters. When the Federation moved its offices off-world, the city fell into disrepair. Though many buildings succumbed to erosion, most of the city remained close to intact years after being abandoned, giving occasional visitors the impression that the city's population simply vanished overnight.<ref name="wizards" />

===Charbi===
{{Main|Charbi}}
Charbi was a polluted city, home to at least one [[Charbi City Spaceport|spaceport]], monitored by the local authorities. By the time of the Second Galactic Civil War, Charbi hosted a meeting between the leaders of the Galactic Alliance and the Confederation. When the Confederation leader was assassinated, the Charbi authorities investigated the murder.<ref name="Sacrificec" />

===Hpaq===
{{Main|Hpaq}}
The city of Hpaq was home to several corporate offices, with companies such as Arakyd Industries and Viper Sensor Intelligence Systems represented.<ref name="HNN" />

===Orbital Advertisement Ring===
{{Main|Orbital Advertisement Ring}}
Stretching all the way around Vulpter, the Orbital Advertisement Ring consisted of enormous advertisement billboards that dominated the skyline of Vulpter. Assorted space debris caught in the Ring only added to its size. The Advertisement Ring cast a shadow large enough to ruin crops on Vulpter's surface, making agriculture even less viable. Every year, the Vulptereens hosted a [[Podracing/Legends|podracing]] event in the Ring.<ref name="wizards" />

==Behind the scenes==
Vulpter was first introduced in the reference book ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Episode I]]'' ([[2000]]), as the homeworld of podracer [[Dud Bolt/Legends|Dud Bolt]]. The planet was slightly elaborated upon in ''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'' ([[2002]]), and received its first appearance in an [[HoloNet News Vol. 531 50|entry]] on the [[HoloNet News (original website)|HoloNet News website]] that same year. It was not until the article ''[[Byss and the Deep Core]]'' ([[2005]]), published as part of [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s [[Planet Hoppers]] feature, that the planet was substantially fleshed out. Vulpter was once again featured in the novel ''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]'' ([[2007]]), and had its location pinpointed by ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' ([[2009]]).
